subject: Service chaining, segmentation, and failover plan for private VPC deployment
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Michael Chen <michael.chen@blueharbor.com>, blueharbor-infra@blueharbor.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service chaining, segmentation, and failover plan for private VPC deployment

Hi Michael / infra team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Attached is a first-pass reference for how Redwood would like to structure the private VPC deployment for BlueHarbor: a separated control plane (CP) subnet, dedicated data plane (DP) worker pools, and an intermediary service-chaining tier for security (ingress/firewall/proxy) and telemetry.

High-level goals:
- CP and DP must be narrowly demarcated: no direct DP access to the public internet; all egress via a controlled proxy chain.
- Service chaining tier handles TLS termination, request routing, and audit logging.
- Failover must be fast (<90s) between primary and standby sites using BGP with health-check-driven route withdraws.

Open questions we want your feedback on:
1) Preferred NAT strategy for the DP: centralized SNAT at the edge vs per-subnet egress nodes?
2) BGP peering details and whether we can accept ASN configuration on your side (we propose private ASN 64520 for the CP-DP fabric).
3) Any regulatory constraints around packet mirroring / telemetry that would block us from egressing logs offsite.

Attached files: service-chaining-v1.drawio.png (diagram), cp-dp-ip-plan.csv (IP plan), runbook-svc-failover.md (draft runbook).

Next step: if you can confirm NAT preference and whether operations want hairpinning disabled, we'll lock the IP plan and schedule a dry-run failover test next week.

Thanks,
Camila
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform
From: Michael Chen <michael.chen@blueharbor.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: blueharbor-infra@blueharbor.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service chaining, segmentation, and failover plan for private VPC deployment

Camila, thanks for the diagram and runbook draft — good level of detail. A few responses inline:

- NAT: we prefer centralized SNAT at the edge for easier egress control and clearer audit trails. That said, central SNAT creates a single failure domain unless paired with active-active pairs and consistent hashing. If you recommend per-subnet egress nodes for availability, we'll need to see the cost/usability tradeoff.

- BGP: we can add the private ASN on our fabric. We'll need the exact BGP community tags you intend to use for automation and for route filtering. Also request that CP announce a specific /24 for control endpoints (we'll advertise on our side for health-check failover).

- Telemetry: packet mirroring offsite is allowed for security team review as long as payloads with PI are redacted. We can sign an NDA addendum if needed.

One operational concern: the service chaining tier should not be a single logical hop for CP->DP control messages. If the chain introduces head-of-line blocking, control plane scale could be impacted. Can we add a bypass ACL for CP->DP control RPCs that preserves audit logging (copy to telemetry stream) but avoids going through full proxy logic?

We can do a sync tomorrow to walk the BGP and NAT specifics.

—Michael
Network Architect, BlueHarbor Systems
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Michael Chen <michael.chen@blueharbor.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service chaining, segmentation, and failover plan for private VPC deployment

On Tue, May 9, 2028 at 11:04 AM Michael Chen wrote:
> One operational concern: the service chaining tier should not be a single logical hop for CP->DP control messages.

Good call — we planned for that. Proposed design: CP->DP control plane RPCs use an explicit route (control-route table) that maps to dedicated control-plane egress nodes (small HA pair) that only run the lightweight control proxy. The heavier service chaining tier (WAF/proxy/telemetry) handles customer-facing ingress and DP traffic.

Key design bullets:
- Control-plane proxies accept TLS mutual auth using client certs pinned to CP instances.
- Control proxies log to an append-only stream; telemetry collectors subscribe rather than inline proxying to avoid CPU spikes.
- Egress NAT: central SNAT at the edge but with active-active pairs in different AZs, symmetric hashing to spread connections. If BlueHarbor wants per-subnet egress, we can provide a template to deploy egress nodes as auto-scaled instances with the same SNAT config.
- Failover: we will advertise health-checked /24s via BGP. On health failure, we withdraw routes; standby announces. Route convergence target: < 60s for data-plane, < 30s for control-plane (control uses faster health-check cadence).

Action items for us:
1) Produce concrete BGP community list and example AS-PATH filters (Karthik).
2) Finalize CP certificate rotation cadence (Laura).
3) Add a short stress test to the runbook to validate control-path latency under load (Aditya).

I'll be on the call tomorrow at 10:00 to walk the BGP bits.

-Markus
Head of Platform Architecture, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, camila.reyes@redwood.com, michael.chen@blueharbor.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 08:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service chaining, segmentation, and failover plan for private VPC deployment

Thanks — I've attached the initial BGP community proposal in the cp-dp-ip-plan.csv and a recommended filter table. Quick notes from the ops perspective:

- We should explicitly block hairpinning on the edge NAT for DP->DP cross-zone flows to avoid asymmetric routing during failover testing. We can enable it temporarily for dry-run windows.
- Health checks: control-plane health probes must be TCP+application-level (RPC ping) to avoid false positives from accepted TCP sockets.
- Smoke test: we'll run a staged failover where we withdraw a single DP /24 and validate that active sessions gracefully reconnect via a keepalive-forwarding approach in the client lib. This will be scripted in runbook-svc-failover.md.

Please review the filters and let me know if BlueHarbor needs any special community tags for automation.

Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: michael.chen@blueharbor.com, blueharbor-infra@blueharbor.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service chaining, segmentation, and failover plan for private VPC deployment

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps: 

Decisions: 
- BlueHarbor: centralized SNAT at edge is acceptable; Redwood will implement active-active SNAT pairs across AZs.
- Control-plane: dedicated control-route table and lightweight control proxies; bypass ACL for CP->DP control RPCs that preserves telemetry copies.
- BGP: BlueHarbor will accept private ASN 64520 and the community/tag list in cp-dp-ip-plan.csv.

Next steps / owners: 
- BlueHarbor infra: confirm community tags + schedule BGP peering (Michael) — target: Thu 10:00 PT.
- Redwood: finalize runbook (Aditya) and add the failover smoke test (Karthik).
- Redwood security: prepare telemetry redaction checklist and NDA addendum (Laura).
- Both: run a dry-run failover (non-production) week of May 15.

I've uploaded the updated diagram and runbook to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3Cservice-chaining-design. Please reply with any blockers; otherwise I'll lock the IP plan at EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Camila
